items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: -- Stewart, and Cootie Williams and all these great musicians.

ctx.x: -- Stewart, and Cootie Williams and all these great musicians. Johnny Hodges, Lawrence Brown. All this was going through my ear and I was fascinated by it. I couldn't get it out of my system. And this is how I really started to listen to jazz music, and during that same time -- of course later on I heard Art Tatum. But much later, it was much later that I heard Art Tatum.

And I would have to say that my first inspiration came to be in the image of Duke Ellington as a writer and composer and pianist, rather than a pianist. And it was not until I heard the great artistry of Art Tatum that I knew that I wanted to become a master of ad lib playing on the piano
